chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:

God, the Mighty and Majestic, did not send any Prophet except with the prohibition of wine, and that he should acknowledge that God does what He wills, and that 'al-kundur' (chewing gum) should be in his inheritance.
He said: And I heard him (peace be upon him) say: Do not enter a dark house at night unless you carry a lamp with you.

key_terms.الْكُنْدُرُ: A type of chewing gum or resin, mentioned here as part of prophetic inheritance

ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of the Prophets according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) highlights three universal markers of Prophethood: the prohibition of wine, the affirmation of God's absolute will, and the specific inheritance of 'al-kundur' (likely a type of garment or fabric). He further adds a practical ethical guideline to enter dark houses at night with a light source, ensuring safety and clarity in daily conduct.
